title: The Jussive Mood (Al-Muḍāriʿ al-Majzūm)
source: Original instructional lesson authored for this application (syllabus ref: Haywood & Nahmad Ch. 16; Ryding Ch. 35)
objectives: Identify jussive governing particles: لَمْ (past negation), لَا النَّاهِيَةُ (prohibition), and conditional إِنْ.
Apply jussive signs: sukūn on sound singulars and deletion of nūn (ḥadhf al-nūn) on al-afʿāl al-khamsah.
Contrast مَا + past tense with لَمْ + jussive.
recallPrompt: From Chapter 15: How do al-afʿāl al-khamsah mark the subjunctive mood?

sections.heading: What Triggers the Jussive (Al-Jazm)?
sections.body: The jussive (al-muḍāriʿ al-majzūm) is a verb-only mood triggered by particles such as لَمْ ('did not' — negating the past using an imperfect stem!), prohibitive لَا ('do not!'), and conditional particles like إِنْ ('if').

sections.label: Jussive Markers
sections.summary: Sound singular stems take sukūn (ـْ) in the jussive; al-afʿāl al-khamsah drop their final nūn; and verbs ending in a weak radical (Chapter 29) delete their final weak letter.

sections.translation: The student did not leave the mosque.
sections.irab: لَمْ: حَرْفُ نَفْيٍ وَجَزْمٍ | يَخْرُجِ: فِعْلٌ مُضَارِعٌ مَجْزُومٌ بِالسُّكُونِ (وَحُرِّكَ بِالكَسْرِ لِالْتِقَاءِ السَّاكِنَيْنِ)
sections.notes: Notice the helping kasrah on يَخْرُجِ before hamzat al-waṣl in الطَّالِبُ to avoid two consecutive vowelless consonants.

sections.heading: Prohibitive لَا vs. Negating لَا
sections.body: لَا تَكْتُبُ (indicative -u) means 'you are not writing'; لَا تَكْتُبْ (jussive sukūn) means 'do not write!'.
